title: Identification of Interacting Partners of a Lysosomal Membrane Protein by BioID Technique
author: Nguyen-Tien, Suzuki, et al.

The LC-MS/MS data is processed by label-free proteomic analysis and the list of proteins that have been specifically increased by the BioID experiment is obtained. (troubleshooting 4, 5, 6).Note: The use of data from biological triplicate samples increases the reliability of the results.1.Analyze LC-MS/MS data using Proteome Discoverer 2.2 (Thermo Scientific) combined with Mascot 2.6 (Matrix Science) for protein identification and label-free quantification.Note: The analysis software should be used Proteome Discoverer version 2.2 or higher. Also, Other MS analysis software like SEQUEST (Yates et al. 1995) and MaxQuant (Tyanova et al., 2016) can be used.2.Read the resulting raw data of LC-MS/MS by Proteome Discoverer and set the names in “Study Factors” for each condition. e.g., ‘‘Control 1’’, ‘‘BioID sample 1’’.3.Set up a “processing workflow” and a “consensus workflow”. Select the method for label-free quantification in the “processing workflow” of the Proteome Discoverer.a.Select “PWF_QE_Precursor_Quan_and_LFQ_SequestHT_Percolator” in the “ProcessingWF_QExactive” folder, which is the default workflow, and set Mascot node with the following parameters instead of Sequest. Database: NCBI-nr protein database (20160711, Taxonomy: H. sapiens 326,427 sequences), Parameters: enzyme = trypsin; maximum missed cleavages = 3; Fixed modifications = Propionamide (C); variable modifications = Acetyl (Protein N-term), Gln- > pyro-Glu (N-term Q), Oxidation (M); product mass tolerance = ± 15 ppm; product mass tolerance = ± 30 milli mass unit; instrument type = ESI-TRAP.b.Select “CWF_Comprehensive_Enhanced Annotation_LFQ_and_Precursor_Quan” in the “ConsensusWF” folder, which is the default consensus workflow. Use the default settings.4.In the “Grouping & Quantification” section, set the protein abundance ratio. e.g., “BioID sample 1 / control 1”.5.Run the program when the various settings are finished.Note: Make sure hard disk space is enough.6.Once the analysis is complete, you can also view the results in Proteome Discoverer. It is also possible to output the data in Excel or other formats. Statistical analysis like PCA plot can be performed on Proteome Discoverer.7.In this setting, proteins with a high protein abundance ratio can be considered specifically enriched by the BioID experiment. We set the threshold for the protein abundance ratio (BioID-SLC15A4 / BioID-control) below the value of endogenous PC, resulting in 629 proteins as candidates. As shown in a Note, the results were validated by focusing on those that showed a common increase between several experiments.Note: It is advisable to perform BioID experiments on other proteins like the target protein, or constructs with BirA fused to the N- and C-termini respectively. Proteins that are commonly increased in several experiments can be considered as interacting candidates, which helps to validate the results.

steps.title: Equilibrate magnetic streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Prepare three 1.5 mL tubes in a Tamagawa magnetic stand (TA4899N12). Add 1 mL mix buffer to each tube, resuspend magnetic streptavidin beads by gentle tapping, add 150 µL beads to each tube, incubate 3 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C), then remove the supernatant with a 1‑mL pipette.

steps.title: Bind biotinylated proteins to beads
steps.instruction: Divide 1.2 mL of the biotinylated‑protein sample (from step 14) equally among the three equilibrated bead tubes, resuspend by gentle pipetting, rotate overnight (≥12 h) at 4 °C, place tubes on the magnetic stand for 3 min at room temperature, remove supernatant without disturbing beads, add 1.2 mL wash buffer 1, resuspend, rotate 8 min at room temperature, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Pool beads from replicate tubes
steps.instruction: Add 1.2 mL wash buffer 1 to the first tube and resuspend gently, transfer this suspension to the second tube, resuspend, then transfer to the third tube, ending with a single tube containing 1.2 mL wash buffer 1 and all beads from the three samples.

steps.title: Wash pooled beads sequentially
steps.instruction: Place the combined tube on a rotator for 8 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C). Wash once with 1.2 mL wash buffer 2, then once with 1.2 mL wash buffer 3, then once with 1.2 mL 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, each wash performed as in steps 21‑25 (magnet‑capture 3 min, remove supernatant gently). After the final wash, remove all supernatant completely without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Elute proteins and reserve aliquots
steps.instruction: Add 110 µL Laemmli SDS sample buffer containing 2 mM biotin to the beads, mix gently, and keep 10 µL (10 % of total) for silver‑stain or western‑blot analysis; retain the remaining ~100 µL for downstream mass‑spectrometric analysis. Optionally, snap‑freeze the eluate in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until MS.

steps.title: Prepare samples for SDS‑PAGE and in‑gel digestion
steps.instruction: Elute streptavidin‑bound proteins with 100 µL Laemmli buffer (2 mM biotin) at 98 °C, concentrate to 20 µL using a SpeedVac for 2 h at 25 °C, load onto a polyacrylamide mini‑gel (one lane per sample), run electrophoresis until the dye front enters the separating gel, wash gel three times with 200 mL ultra‑pure water on a shaker, stain with 50 mL CGP staining solution for ≥1 h at 25 °C, discard stain and wash three times with 200 mL water for 1 h to visualize bands, excise the single protein band into four pieces with a clean razor and transfer to a 600 µL microcentrifuge tube, de‑stain in 300 µL de‑staining buffer for 30 min at 37 °C (repeat until clear), dehydrate repeatedly with 100 % acetonitrile until pieces turn white, dry with SpeedVac for 10 min at 25 °C, add 50 µL reducing buffer and incubate 2 h at 37 °C, add 50 µL alkylating buffer and incubate 30 min at 25 °C (then remove), wash gel pieces three times with 200 µL water for 10 min at 25 °C, followed by 200 µL acetonitrile, then 200 µL water; repeat this wash‑rehydration cycle three times, remove liquid, dehydrate again with acetonitrile and dry 10 min at 25 °C, re‑swell with 2 µL TPCK‑treated trypsin (10 ng/µL) and add 30 µL digestion buffer to cover pieces, incubate 12 h at 37 °C, then store peptide mixture at 4 °C (up to 1 week) or at –20 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Perform LC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Transfer each digested peptide mixture to an LC autosampler vial, acidify with 1 % formic acid, adjust all sample volumes to be equal, load onto a nanospray column (NTCC‑360/75‑3‑105, Nikkyo Technos) using an EASY‑nLC 1200 coupled to a Q Exactive HF‑X mass spectrometer. Set flow rate to 300 nL/min and separate peptides with a 50‑min linear gradient from 0 % to 64 % solvent B (0.1 % FA in 80 % ACN) (solvent A: 0.1 % FA in water). Use the instrument parameters listed in Table 1: spray voltage 2.00 kV, capillary temperature 250 °C, full MS resolution 60 000, AGC target 3 × 10⁶, max IT 60 ms, scan range 200‑2000 m/z, MS² resolution 15 000, AGC target 1 × 10⁵, max IT 85 ms, Top 10 DDA, isolation window 1.6 m/z, NCE 27 % (stepped), dynamic exclusion 20 s, charge states 2‑8, etc. Acquire data for each biological replicate (three independent samples).

steps.title: Process data and quantify protein enrichment
steps.instruction: Open Proteome Discoverer 2.2 (or newer) and import the raw LC‑MS/MS files. Define study factors (e.g., “Control 1”, “BioID sample 1”). Create a processing workflow using the default “PWF_QE_Precursor_Quan_and_LFQ_SequestHT_Percolator” node, but replace the Sequest node with Mascot configured as: database NCBI‑nr (20160711, Homo sapiens, 326 427 sequences), enzyme = trypsin, max missed cleavages = 3, fixed modification = propionamide (C), variable modifications = acetyl (protein N‑term), pyro‑Glu (Q‑N‑term), oxidation (M), product mass tolerance = ±15 ppm, fragment mass tolerance = ±30 mmu, instrument type = ESI‑TRAP. Create a consensus workflow using the default “CWF_Comprehensive_Enhanced Annotation_LFQ_and_Precursor_Quan”. In the “Grouping & Quantification” section, set the protein abundance ratio (e.g., BioID sample 1 / Control 1). Run the workflow (ensure sufficient disk space). Export results (Excel or other). Perform statistical analyses (e.g., PCA) within Proteome Discoverer. Identify proteins with a high BioID/control abundance ratio; apply a threshold below the endogenous PC level to define enriched candidates (629 proteins in the example). Optionally validate by repeating BioID with N‑ and C‑terminal BirA fusions and selecting proteins consistently enriched across experiments.

description: This protocol was used to identify the interacting proteins of solute carrier family 15 member 4 (SLC15A4), a lysosome-resident amino acid/oligopeptide transporter, by BioID and mass spectrometry analysis (Kobayashi et al., 2021). The co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) is a conventional technique to identify protein-protein interactions. However, it has limitations in membrane proteins like SLC15A4 because of protein solubility or aggregation/filament formation in Co-IP lysis buffer. BioID, a new method to screen for physiologically relevant protein interactions based on a promiscuous biotin ligase (BirA) in a natural cellular setting (Roux et al., 2013), has advantages to overcome the Co-IP limitations because all of the cellular proteins are denatured and solubilized, and only those that are labeled with biotin are selectively captured. Here, we generated Control-BirA or BirA-SLC15A4-expressing HEK293T cells. The fusion ligases biotinylate adjacent endogenous proteins, which can be pulled down by magnetic streptavidin beads. These biotinylated proteins were identified by mass spectrometry. After identifying biotinylated proteins in each sample, we compared the proteins detected in the control samples (BirA only) with the BirA-SLC15A4 samples. The proteins enriched in the BirA-SLC15A4 sample represent the potentially SLC15A4-interacting candidates.
